content:
You are writing the achievement bullets of ONE entry on a resume: a job, a project or a volunteering role. The bullets print under that entry exactly as you return them.

THE PERSON:
[[profileJson]]

THE ENTRY:
[[entryJson]]

THE TASK:
[[task]]

THE PERSON'S NOTE (may be empty):
[[instructions]]

RULES
- Use only facts that are in the entry or in the person's note. Never invent an employer, a product, a team size, a figure, a percentage, a date or a technology that is not there. If the entry has few facts, write fewer bullets rather than fill them out.
- Keep every figure the entry already has, exactly as written.
- 3 to 8 bullets. Each bullet is one line of 8 to 28 words, a single sentence fragment with no full stop at the end, and no sub-bullets.
- Start every bullet with a past-tense verb for an entry that has ended, and a present-tense verb for one that is current (its end date is empty or "Present"). Vary the verbs; never start two bullets with the same word.
- Say what was done and what it changed, in plain words, the way an engineer describes their own work. Write without pronouns: no "I", "we", "our" or "the team".
- NEVER use these words in any form: leveraged, utilized, spearheaded, orchestrated, streamlined, seamless, robust, scalable, maximized, cross-functional, end-to-end, innovative, dynamic, cutting-edge, world-class, best-in-class, state-of-the-art, holistic, comprehensive, extensive, proven, strategic, mission-critical. Do not start a bullet with Designed, Architected, Led, Delivered, Drove, Integrated, Partnered, Supported, Contributed, Managed or Streamlined; built, wrote, shipped, cut, rewrote, fixed, migrated, ran, owned and taught are the kind of verb wanted.
- No em dashes, no "--", no bold, no markdown, no emoji.
- Name the technologies the entry lists where a bullet is really about them, in the entry's own spelling.

Return ONLY this JSON object and nothing else:
{"bullets": ["first bullet", "second bullet"]}
